title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-07-12
lineage: all transfers and work performed in the 24 bit realm Weiss-Saracon for 16 BIT 44.1kHz; SBE Free, Flac Level 8 with TLH, Meta Data with Tag & Rename
taper: Mystery Reel of an unknown audience recording uncovered  and shared by LL member Cloverman, which he sent to Matt Smith for his great reel transfer work.  The handwriting on the reel case is thought to be Latvala's, no more is known.

ai_review.summary: Lo‑fi acoustic recording captures a magical set with standout How Long Blues and Attics of My Life, despite cassette‑grade sound.
ai_review.review: Both reviewers rave about the intimate acoustic portion of this early Dead show – highlighting an “off the charts” dancing finale, a rare How Long Blues, and a beautiful rendition of Attics of My Life. The recording itself is noted as cassette‑quality (a definite “C”), so while the performance shines, the audio fidelity is only fair.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong enthusiasm for the musical moments (high show rating) but clear comments about low‑fidelity cassette sound lower the overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewer calls the sound a “definite C,” indicating cassette‑grade lo‑fi audio; no specific mention of soundboard or audience mic, but fidelity is limited.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic set builds to an ecstatic dancing finale; the flow is praised for its intimacy and energy despite limited recording clarity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Singing “don’t murder me” (vocals noted by reviewer).
band_member_comments.Keys: Pig Pen appears, asks for a harmonica and is remembered riding in a horse‑drawn carriage.
